summary: Request to run an AI-grid flood (reachability flood fill) on a level: pointer to the eoc::AiFlood result object, level name, flood flags and three integer parameters. Consumed by eoc::aigrid::FloodRequestSystem (game per-frame update bg3.exe+0xF2C0B0, ProcessNewRequests bg3.exe+0xF2C150; Toolkit EoCShared.dll+0xE4B9C0), which calls eoc::AiGrid::RequestFlood(AiFlood*, Flags<EAiFloodFlag> const&, int, int, int) and stores the returned request handle in eoc::aigrid::_private::FloodRequestStateComponent. eoc::controller::FloodComponent holds the same pointer/handle/level trio on the client. Never seen alive. Registry total 32 (client and server rows).

fields.name: Flood
fields.evidence: Game ProcessNewRequests bg3.exe+0xF2C150 (storage stride 0x20): reads the 8-byte value at +0 of the request as the flood object pointer; it writes the flood object's +0x54 (uint16 flags), +0x56 (byte 0) and +0x58 (int) and stores that pointer into the new AiGrid request. Toolkit ProcessNewRequests passes the 8-byte value at +0 of the request as the AiFlood* argument of AiGrid::RequestFlood. macOS default: zero.

fields.name: Level
fields.evidence: Toolkit ProcessNewRequests passes the address +8 of the request as the FixedString argument of LevelManager::GetLevel, and has the assert 'Trying to request a flood on unexisting level '%s''. Game: the 32-bit value at +8 of the request is hashed and compared as the level-map key. macOS default stores a null FixedString at +8.

fields.name: Flags
fields.evidence: Game ProcessNewRequests copies the 2-byte value at +0xC of the request to AiFlood+0x54; Toolkit passes the address +0xC of the request as the ls::Flags<eoc::EAiFloodFlag,0,33> const& argument of AiGrid::RequestFlood, which copies 2 bytes to AiFlood+0x54. Enum eoc::EAiFloodFlag (written as uint16). macOS default writes a 16-bit value at +0xC.

fields.name: _PadE
fields.evidence: alignment of the int at +0x10; not read.

fields.name: field_10
fields.evidence: Game ProcessNewRequests: reads the 8-byte value at +0x10 of the request and stores its low 32 bits (the int at +0x10) at AiGrid request +0x14. Toolkit: passed as the first int of RequestFlood (to EoCShared.dll+0xE32D60). macOS default writes one 8-byte store at +0x10 that covers +0x10..+0x17.

fields.name: field_14
fields.evidence: Game: the 32-bit value at +0x14 of the request is stored at AiGrid request +0x10. Toolkit: second int of RequestFlood.

fields.name: field_18
fields.evidence: Game: reads the int at +0x18 of the request, clamps 0x7FFFFFFF to 0x7FFFFFFE and writes it to AiFlood+0x58 (Toolkit RequestFlood does the same with its last int) - probably a maximum distance/cost of the flood. macOS default writes a 32-bit value at +0x18.

fields.name: _Pad1C
fields.evidence: padding to the 8-aligned size 0x20; not read.

open_questions: Meaning of the three ints (+0x10, +0x14, +0x18) beyond where they go; AiGrid::RequestFlood's parameters are unnamed.
No Windows creator with defaults was found (only registration helpers bg3.exe+0x1454C0/0xE6710); the component is probably added by script/Osiris code with full values.
Flood is an owning pointer to eoc::AiFlood (0x100-byte object with a virtual destructor, see eoc::controller::FloodComponent) - kept as void*.
Not seen alive (seen.py has no samples).
